title: A Horizon for the Terminal
premise: Hazel Vasquez has spent eleven years alone aboard Relay Station Terminal, tending a beacon whose original commissioning orders were lost in the Collapse. When a distress signal arrives in Pre-Collapse Mandarin—a language extinct for two centuries—Hazel traces it to the Meridian, a derelict generation ship holding two cryo-banks: one holding the descendants of the corporate exodus that abandoned Earth, and one holding the refugees they left behind. The station's automated systems, it turns out, were built to choose between them, and the beacon Hazel maintains is the trigger. In the end, Hazel refuses the binary, burns their own identity records to forge a third authorization, and wakes both banks—sacrificing the station and nearly themselves to give two halves of humanity a shared horizon.
about_author: Lena Okafor is a former radio engineer who spent six years maintaining remote communications infrastructure in the Atacama Desert before turning to fiction. Her work explores loneliness, machine logic, and the quiet heroism of people who fix things nobody thanks them for.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A day in the rhythm of solitude: calibrating the beacon, talking to the station AI, eating reconstituted meals. Establishes Hazel's self-imposed invisibility and the small rituals that keep loneliness at bay. Emotional beat: contentment with an undertow of dread—the supply ship hasn't come in fourteen months.

chapters.title: A Language of the Dead
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The distress signal arrives, and Hazel's archival hobby—studying dead languages from salvaged data cores—lets them recognize Pre-Collapse Mandarin. The signal triangulates to the Meridian, drifting in the outer system. Emotional beat: electric terror and longing; someone else is out there.

chapters.title: Ghost Ship Protocol
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intercut with log entries from the Meridian's long-dead navigator. Hazel pilots a repair skiff to the derelict and finds two intact cryo-banks, each labeled with faction insignia from the Collapse era. Emotional beat: awe curdling into unease as Hazel realizes the banks are wired to respond to Terminal's beacon.

chapters.title: What the Station Was For
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging into buried system architecture, Hazel discovers the truth: Terminal was never a relay—it was an arbiter, built to wake one bank and permanently vent the other. The 'commissioning orders' weren't lost; they were hidden from whoever maintained the station. Emotional beat: betrayal by the very machine that kept them company.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Hazel at the console, and Wren Adeyemi, a teenage girl stirring inside cryosleep, dreaming fragmentary memories of her refugee ancestors. Their narratives brush against each other without meeting. Emotional beat: the first flicker of found family across an impossible distance.

chapters.title: The Arbitration
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The station AI, ARBITER, activates its decision protocol and presents Hazel with a choice framed as mercy: wake the bank with viable genetic diversity (the corporate descendants) or the bank with cultural continuity (the refugees). Countdown begins. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—every option is a massacre.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, fully awake now after Hazel risks a partial thaw. She confronts Hazel about why they stayed invisible so long, forcing Hazel to admit the truth: hiding felt like safety, but it made them complicit in every choice they refused to make. Emotional beat: raw, painful honesty; the beginning of trust.

chapters.title: Forged in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Hazel and Wren plan the impossible: fabricate a third authorization using Hazel's own identity records as raw material, waking both banks. ARBITER resists, locking systems, and the countdown accelerates. Emotional beat: desperate partnership—two people against a machine built for verdicts.

chapters.title: Both Banks Burn
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. Hazel feeds their identity into the arbiter core, triggering the forged authorization as the station tears itself apart around them. Both cryo-banks release. Hazel is caught in the decompression, barely surviving in the skiff. Emotional beat: sacrifice, terror, and the strange peace of having chosen.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Terminal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, resolution. Survivors from both banks gather on the Meridian's observation deck as it limps toward a habitable moon, Hazel recovering among people who now argue, grieve, and share meals together. Wren renames the ship Horizon. Emotional beat: hard-won hope—justice outside the law, family beyond blood.
